_comment: Every REPLACE_ME below is a value only the team can supply — see docs/PREREQUISITES.md. The deploy workflow refuses to run while any of them survives, so a half-filled file fails loudly instead of deploying something wrong. NB the guard reads the VALUES of keys that do not start with an underscore, so a comment may say REPLACE_ME (this one does) — but a comment stored under a NORMAL key would refuse every deploy. Keep documentation under `_`-prefixed keys.
_comment_ingresses: ONE hostname, a full https:// URL. It feeds spec.ingresses, and MUNINN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is DERIVED from it in app.yaml — there is deliberately no second variable to keep in step. `ansatt.dev.nav.no` was dropped: that domain authenticates through a shared SSO client, which leaves this app's group gate out of the login. See docs/PREREQUISITES.md §4.
_comment_admins: There is deliberately no `admin_oids` key: an oid is a stable personal identifier for a named human, and this repo is public. MUNINN_ADMIN_IDENTS comes from the nais secret named below, which somebody creates in the namespace out of band — see docs/PREREQUISITES.md §10. The secret is named after the APP, which is what melosys-console-q2 does (envFrom: [{secret: melosys-console-q2}]) — nais's own generated secrets are prefixed, e.g. azure-melosys-muninn-q2-…, so there is nothing to collide with. The secret's KEY must be literally MUNINN_ADMIN_IDENTS; envFrom injects keys verbatim.
_comment_vertex: There is deliberately no `vertex_host` key. The egress host is DERIVED by the deploy workflow from gcp_project + vertex_region and passed to nais/deploy as a VAR — leave it out and it stays that way. Adding it back means either a REPLACE_ME the first run hard-fails on, or a hand-filled value the computed VAR silently overrides.
_comment_db: There is deliberately no `db_instance` key. The instance name is left unset in app.yaml so it defaults to the APP name — melosys-muninn-q2, which already carries the environment — matching skattehendelser-q2 and both faktureringskomponenten apps. `db_name` carries the -q2 suffix for the same reason: a prod deployment must not want a name this one already holds.
